title: Lesson 7: Spiritual Warfare and Putting on the Armor of God
description: The Christian life is not a stroll through a quiet park. It is a battle, and you are already in it. This lesson will help you understand the real enemy you face, the armor God has given you, and how to stand firm every single day.

blocks.text: In the last lesson, you saw how to live for Jesus at work and school. Here is something every believer needs to hear plainly: living on mission meets resistance. Not only a full calendar or an awkward conversation, but a real spiritual enemy who hates what God is doing in you and through you. This lesson is about the battle you are already in, and the armor God has already given you to stand.
Sent into the Battle

blocks.alt: Jesus, in the foreground, sends His followers out two by two as they walk farther down a long road toward the villages

blocks.title: Jesus Sends the 72
blocks.text: Before Paul ever wrote about armor, Jesus sent His followers into a real spiritual battle. In Luke 10, He sent seventy-two of them out two by two, carrying nothing extra, speaking peace over every house, announcing that the kingdom of God had come near. They went in His name and with His authority, holding nothing but what He had told them. When they came back, they could hardly believe what had happened.

The seventy-two returned with joy, saying, "Lord, even the demons are subject to us in your name!" And he said to them, "I saw Satan fall like lightning from heaven. Behold, I have given you authority to tread on serpents and scorpions, and over all the power of the enemy, and nothing shall hurt you. Nevertheless, do not rejoice in this, that the spirits are subject to you, but rejoice that your names are written in heaven."

Look at what Jesus does. His followers have just seen demons submit to them, and He does not say "good job." He says, "Do not rejoice in this." Rejoice instead that your names are written in heaven. He points them away from the power they felt and toward the identity they already had. That is the heart of spiritual warfare. You are not fighting to earn a place with God. You are fighting from the place He has already given you.
7.1 - When have you felt real spiritual resistance while trying to follow Jesus or serve others?
Dress for the Battle You Are Already In
Years later Paul, writing as a prisoner in chains and perhaps with a Roman soldier a few feet away, gave the church a picture of what Jesus' followers were already living.

Finally, be strong in the Lord and in the strength of his might. Put on the whole armor of God, that you may be able to stand against the schemes of the devil. For we do not wrestle against flesh and blood, but against the rulers, against the authorities, against the cosmic powers over this present darkness, against the spiritual forces of evil in the heavenly places. Therefore take up the whole armor of God, that you may be able to withstand in the evil day, and having done all, to stand firm. Stand therefore, having fastened on the belt of truth, and having put on the breastplate of righteousness, and, as shoes for your feet, having put on the readiness given by the gospel of peace. In all circumstances, take up the shield of faith, with which you can extinguish all the flaming darts of the evil one; and take the helmet of salvation, and the sword of the Spirit, which is the word of God, praying at all times in the Spirit, with all prayer and supplication.

Notice what Paul does not say. He does not say "go find some armor." He says put on the whole armor of God. This is not a try-harder speech. It is a be-dependent command. God supplies every piece. Your job is to put it on.
One Piece at a Time

The belt of truth keeps you from tripping over the enemy's oldest trick, a twisted version of what God said. The breastplate of righteousness covers your heart, and it is Christ's righteousness, not your good behavior, so it holds. The shoes of the gospel of peace keep your feet planted and move you out on mission. The shield of faith puts out the fiery thoughts: doubt, fear, shame, discouragement. The helmet of salvation guards what you believe about your security in Christ; remember, your name is written in heaven. And the sword of the Spirit, the Word of God, is the one piece that fights back.
7.2 - Which piece of armor do you most often forget to put on?
A Sword for the Lie

Five of the six pieces are for defense. The sword is different. When Jesus was tempted in the wilderness, He did not argue with the devil or lean on willpower. He said, "It is written." Three times the devil attacked, and three times Jesus answered with Scripture. You do not fight lies with feelings. You fight lies with truth. But you cannot draw a sword you do not carry, and that is why knowing your Bible matters so much. Most of the enemy's darts are sentences. Each one has a verse that answers it.

blocks.title: A Sword for the Lie
content: "God has forgotten you." "I will never leave you nor forsake you" (Hebrews 13:5).
"You will never change." "He who began a good work in you will bring it to completion at the day of Jesus Christ" (Philippians 1:6).
"You are a fraud and a failure." "There is therefore now no condemnation for those who are in Christ Jesus" (Romans 8:1).

blocks.text: 7.3 - Which lie do you hear most often, and what verse answers it?
Stand Together, Stand Firm

Paul finishes the armor and goes straight to prayer: "praying at all times in the Spirit, with all prayer and supplication" (Ephesians 6:18). Prayer is how you put the armor on. And every "you" in this passage is plural. Paul wrote to a church, not a lone soldier, and he even asked them to pray that he would speak the gospel boldly. You were never meant to stand alone. Pray for the believers around you by name, and let them pray for you. When one of you is under fire, the others stand close.

Paul uses the word stand four times. Stand against the schemes. Withstand in the evil day. Having done all, stand firm. Stand therefore. The armor is not about becoming a spiritual hero. It is daily dependence on a God who has already won the war. The Lord who sent out the seventy-two and told them to rejoice that their names are written in heaven is the same Lord who sends you. Your call is simply to stand.
This Week's Practice

Each morning this week, before you look at your phone, pray through the armor one piece at a time: Lord, I put on the belt of Your truth. I put on the breastplate of Christ's righteousness, not my own. Keep going through the shoes, the shield, the helmet, and the sword. It takes about two minutes. Then pick the lie you hear most and memorize the verse that answers it. That is your sword for the week, and it is one you can hand to someone else.
7.4 - Who in your life is under fire right now, and which verse could you hand them this week?
Lesson 7 Review

Living on mission meets real spiritual resistance, but you do not fight to earn a place with God. You fight from the place He has already given you. God supplies the whole armor, and you put it on in prayer, standing with other believers rather than alone. The enemy's darts are mostly lies, and for every lie there is a sword: a verse that answers it. Jesus has already won, so your call is simply to stand.
In the next lesson, you will learn how to walk alongside someone else and help them grow as a follower of Jesus.
